assumptions: completeness and downward self-reducibility give the hard function structure a random function lacks
a lower-bound argument can consume that rare structure instead of a broadly shared property
operators: hardness condensation onto one function family

proposal.structural_violation_claim: The weakened candidates record that every failed circuit-program attempt preserved a large, efficiently certifiable distinguishing property, and the natural-proofs wall condemns exactly the conjunction of largeness and constructivity. This direction keeps constructivity but deliberately breaks largeness: build the distinguishing property from structure essentially only the target family possesses — the downward self-reducibility and completeness of SAT itself — so the property holds for a negligible fraction of functions and cannot serve as a pseudorandom-function distinguisher. A hypothesis about which conserved feature is load-bearing (largeness), not a verified escape.
proposal.novelty_argument: Distinct from the recorded escape-space occupant (orbit-closure obstructions), which also chooses rarity but pays with open representation-theoretic problems and an unestablished algebraic-to-Boolean transfer. Here the rare structure is native to the Boolean question, so no transfer obligation exists. Distinct from the post-natural-proofs decade's attempts, recorded as varying the property while keeping it large. Remaining obligations: exhibit one concrete circuit-class consequence of self-reducibility that small circuits cannot mimic, and prove the property's rarity formally.
proposal.cheapest_falsification_path: Naturalization audit: re-run the draft argument on a random function with the self-reducibility hypothesis deleted. If the argument survives, the property was secretly large and the natural-proofs wall applies; the direction fails. A second cheap check: exhaustively compute the property's density on tiny truth tables (n<=4) to confirm rarity before investing further.

assumptions: unconditional deterministic identity tests are achievable for structured subclasses (bounded depth, bounded top fan-in, read restrictions)
the algorithm-to-hardness bridge instantiates on restricted classes with correspondingly restricted lower-bound conclusions
auxiliary_objects: hitting sets for depth-bounded arithmetic circuits

proposal.structural_violation_claim: The recorded boundary of the bridge (pnp-11) is that it is conditional in the wrong direction: its hypothesis, deterministic subexponential identity testing, is open in full generality. The proposed move attacks the hypothesis incrementally rather than accepting or refuting it wholesale: supply unconditional deterministic identity tests for progressively richer restricted arithmetic classes, and determine for each whether a restricted version of the implication already yields an unconditional lower-bound consequence. That any restricted instantiation of the bridge produces an unconditional consequence is a hypothesis; the obligation is both the algorithm and a re-derivation of the implication under the restriction.
proposal.novelty_argument: Nearest family: the derandomization bridge itself (pnp-11). The difference is operational, not terminological: pnp-11 as recorded consumes a hypothesis nobody can supply, whereas this program manufactures partial hypotheses and asks what each one buys, converting a single all-or-nothing conditional into a ladder of unconditional sub-results. Unlike the circuit program (pnp-03 through pnp-06), progress is measured in algorithms delivered, not properties found, so pnp-08 does not bind.
proposal.cheapest_falsification_path: Attempt an explicit hitting set for the smallest nontrivial class (depth-3 arithmetic circuits with constant top fan-in) and, in parallel, re-derive the bridge implication under that restriction. Failure modes are cheap to observe: either the restricted hitting set resists construction for the same reason general PIT does, or the restricted implication yields only conclusions already known unconditionally, in which case the ladder has no first rung and the direction is abandoned.

representations: compressed or sparse versions of NP problems
assumptions: slightly-superlinear bounds for compressed problem versions imply strong bounds for the original problem
the weak-bound regime is reachable by existing restricted-model techniques

proposal.structural_violation_claim: The recorded failures conserve the expectation that the analyzed object is the full model at full scale and that only superpolynomial bounds count as progress. This direction inverts the target: prove only a barely superlinear bound for a compressed/sparse version of an NP-complete problem, plus an amplification theorem showing such a weak bound already implies a strong separation. The departure is in where the proof burden sits — a quantitatively tiny bound in a local regime — with the amplifier, a reduction-theoretic object rather than a distinguishing property, carrying the leap. The amplifier's own preserved properties are the unverified part.
proposal.novelty_argument: No recorded program attacks the quantitative-weakness frontier this way: the time-space program produced weak bounds with no amplifier; the circuit program sought strong bounds directly. Remaining obligations: (a) prove an amplification statement of the required strength; (b) prove the weak compressed-version bound; (c) verify the amplifier does not smuggle the full difficulty into (b).
proposal.cheapest_falsification_path: Barrier-relocation audit: instantiate the amplifier on a model with known complexity and check whether the weak-bound hypothesis it demands is already blocked by relativization or naturalization at the weak scale. If the hypothesis regime inherits the walls, the amplifier only relocated the difficulty and the direction fails — bookkeeping only, no new lower bound needed.

representations: non-constructive existence arguments over truth-table properties
assumptions: a distinguishing property need not be efficiently decidable to power a lower bound
counting or incompressibility arguments can certify small circuits lack the property without a poly(truth-table)-time tester

proposal.structural_violation_claim: The conserved property across the circuit-program failures is a distinguishing property that is both large and constructive. This direction breaks the constructivity half: use properties defined by incompressibility or capacity counting whose membership is not efficiently decidable, established existentially rather than by a tester. The natural-proofs reduction needs an efficient distinguisher; a non-constructive property does not supply one. It also departs the conserved deterministic uncertainty mode, since the existence arguments are counting-based. A hypothesized departure, not a proven evasion.
proposal.novelty_argument: The atlas records the escape space (non-constructive or rare) as mapped and, through 2004, occupied only by the orbit-closure program on the rarity horn. This takes the other horn, non-constructivity, which no recorded program occupies. It differs from bare function-counting because the stated obligation is exactly the gap to close: converting a non-constructive largeness argument into hardness of an explicit function, e.g. via a downward-translation or padding step trading explicitness for class strength. That obligation is stated, not discharged.
proposal.cheapest_falsification_path: (1) For the first candidate property, attempt to write a polynomial-time truth-table tester directly; success means the property naturalizes and the departure is falsified immediately. (2) Check the explicitness-conversion step on a class with known answers (AC0): if the non-constructive route cannot re-derive the known explicit AC0 bound, the conversion step is broken and the direction fails.

representations: non-constructive counting arguments over truth tables
assumptions: the escape space mapped by the natural-proofs barrier (non-constructive or rare properties) contains a usable property besides the GCT occupant
non-constructivity can be certified rather than merely suspected
operators: property search restricted to the mapped escape space

proposal.structural_violation_claim: The recorded decade after the natural-proofs barrier (pnp-09) shows attempts that re-encountered the largeness/constructivity trap because candidate properties were never screened against the barrier before investment. The proposed move makes the barrier itself an operator: every candidate distinguishing property for a strong class is first run through the property-to-distinguisher reduction of pnp-08 as a mandatory filter, and only candidates that provably fail to yield a PRF distinguisher are pursued. That the filtered space is non-empty for TC0-level classes is a hypothesis; the obligation for any surviving candidate is a full lower-bound derivation, and survival of the filter is not evidence of success.
proposal.novelty_argument: Nearest families: the post-natural-proofs attempts (pnp-09) and GCT (pnp-10). Unlike pnp-09's attempts, which are recorded as conserving the trapped posture in new vocabulary, the mechanism here changes the search procedure, not just the candidates: the barrier is used generatively as a screening oracle rather than encountered post hoc. Unlike pnp-10, no commitment is made to representation theory; the escape space is searched broadly with the filter as the only fixed element, so failure localizes to candidates rather than to the whole program.
proposal.cheapest_falsification_path: Formalize the filter as a checkable schema and run the three known lower-bound properties (pnp-03, pnp-04, pnp-06) through it; each must be correctly flagged as natural, otherwise the filter is broken and the direction fails immediately. Then test whether the GCT obstruction posture (rare multiplicity obstructions, pnp-10) passes; if even the one known escape-space occupant is rejected, the filter is too strong and must be repaired or abandoned before any new search is funded.

representations: algebraic proof systems over composite-modulus rings
assumptions: the circuit-program stall at composite moduli and the proof-program stall at counting-capable systems share one mechanism
degree lower bounds over rings with composite modulus are provable in restricted cases

proposal.structural_violation_claim: The atlas records two independent stalls at the same expressiveness level — composite-modulus gates (pnp-06) and counting-capable proof systems (pnp-07) — but records no attempt to treat them as one object. The proposed move studies algebraic proof systems over composite-modulus rings directly, where both stalls coexist in a single analyzable system, to either extract the shared obstruction as a theorem or find that the stalls are distinct. The claim of a shared mechanism is explicitly a hypothesis inferred from the recorded parallel, not an established invariant. This direction knowingly retains the large-constructive-property posture, so any bound it produces is confined to systems below the pnp-08 threshold; its value is diagnostic — locating the shared wall precisely — rather than separational, and the remaining obligation is a degree lower bound over Z_m for composite m in even one restricted subsystem.
proposal.novelty_argument: Nearest families: AC0[p] algebraic approximation (pnp-06) and resolution lower bounds (pnp-07). The recorded programs each climbed their own hierarchy; the mechanism here is the cross-program fusion object — a proof system whose lines are polynomials over a composite-modulus ring — which appears in neither entry. The move is not a terminology change because the analyzed object (refutations over Z_m) is syntactically and semantically distinct from both circuits over F_p and resolution clauses, and the target theorem (a shared-obstruction characterization) is a new claim type in the atlas.
proposal.cheapest_falsification_path: Attempt a degree lower bound for the pigeonhole tautology in a polynomial-calculus-style system over Z_6. If standard degree arguments transfer unchanged from the prime case, the composite-modulus obstruction is not proof-theoretically visible and the shared-mechanism hypothesis is weakened at the cost of one exercise. If instead the argument fails at the same step where the pnp-06 polynomial representation fails, that is positive diagnostic evidence worth recording either way.

assumptions: occurrence obstructions or multiplicity gaps exist at computationally reachable parameters
small-case data can confirm or kill the obstruction hypothesis before deep theory is built

proposal.structural_violation_claim: The orbit-closure program is recorded as the sole occupant of the mapped escape space but stalled as a posture with no extracted bound, its obligations parked inside open multiplicity problems handled deterministically and existentially. This direction departs that conserved handling: attack the obligations empirically and probabilistically, computing multiplicities at small parameters and randomly searching module space for one concrete occurrence obstruction, converting open-problem debt into falsifiable finite computations. The conserved property departed from, in ordinary words, is treating obstructions as objects to classify in full generality before exhibiting any instance.
proposal.novelty_argument: Same representation-theoretic frame as the recorded program, but the operator set shifts from symmetry classification to explicit finite computation and randomized search, and the uncertainty mode shifts from deterministic to probabilistic — producing different artifacts (finite multiplicity tables, found-or-not obstruction candidates) with different failure semantics, so this is a mechanism change rather than terminology. Remaining obligation, stated openly: a found small-parameter obstruction proves nothing asymptotic; a separate lifting argument is owed.
proposal.cheapest_falsification_path: Run the finite computation at the smallest nontrivial parameters and compare candidate-module multiplicities between the two orbit closures. If exhaustive small-parameter search finds no multiplicity gap where the program's heuristics predict one, that is direct evidence the obstruction hypothesis fails at reachable scales, and the direction is deprioritized without any asymptotic theory being built. The computation is bounded and checkable by independent re-execution.

assumptions: arithmetization provides non-black-box leverage that pure simulation lacks
algebraic self-correction of polynomial encodings composes with hierarchy-theorem machinery

proposal.structural_violation_claim: The time-space tradeoff family (pnp-12) is recorded as largely relativizing and therefore wall-bounded by the contrary oracles of pnp-02. The proposed move injects arithmetization — replacing black-box query behavior with low-degree polynomial encodings of computation transcripts — into the assumption-to-contradiction pipeline, so at least one step inspects algebraic structure an oracle cannot preserve. The claim that this strictly enlarges the reachable bounds beyond the recorded small-exponent cap is a hypothesis; the remaining obligation is to prove a single new unconditional bound (even a slightly larger time-space exponent for satisfiability) whose proof demonstrably fails under some shared oracle.
proposal.novelty_argument: Nearest family: indirect diagonalization (pnp-12), which the atlas records as preserving black-box relativizing simulation. The mechanistic difference is a change in the preserved-property set, not vocabulary: the argument's inner simulation step is replaced by algebraic evaluation of encoded transcripts, an operation absent from every entry in the atlas's diagonalization lineage (pnp-01, pnp-12). It also differs from the circuit-analysis flank (pnp-03 through pnp-06) because no distinguishing property over a circuit class is exhibited, so the naturalness trap of pnp-08 does not apply.
proposal.cheapest_falsification_path: Before seeking new bounds, run the barrier test: attempt to construct an oracle-like algebraic extension world in which arithmetization-augmented arguments still hold but the target separation fails. If such a world exists, the hybrid is condemned by the same schema as pnp-02 and the direction fails cheaply. If not, attempt to reprove the weakest known time-space bound with the algebraic inner step and check whether the exponent cap moves at all; no movement on the smallest case is failure evidence.

representations: succinct or compressed versions of satisfiability
assumptions: for suitably compressed problems, slightly superlinear lower bounds in weak models imply strong separations for the uncompressed problem
the transfer failure of the monotone program is a property of that restriction, not of transfer as such

proposal.structural_violation_claim: The recorded transfer failure (pnp-05) shows a specific bridge — monotone bounds to general bounds — severed by an exponential gap. The proposed move inverts where the strength is demanded: instead of proving strong bounds in a weak model and hoping the restriction is inessential, identify problem/model pairs where provably weak (barely superlinear) bounds already amplify through padding and completeness into superpolynomial general bounds. The existence of such amplification thresholds for natural compressed problems is a hypothesis; the obligation is to prove the amplification lemma itself unconditionally and locate a weak bound above the threshold.
proposal.novelty_argument: Nearest family: the monotone-to-general transfer hope (pnp-05). It is mechanistically distinct because the failed program transferred a bound across models at fixed strength, whereas this transfers across strength at a carefully chosen problem encoding — the load-bearing object is the translation lemma, not the restricted-model lower bound. It is also distinct from pure padding arguments in the diagonalization lineage (pnp-01) because the amplification must be non-black-box in the problem encoding to avoid the pnp-02 schema.
proposal.cheapest_falsification_path: Prove or refute the amplification implication for one toy case: a sparse or succinctly-encoded language and a weak model where near-linear bounds are already provable. If every provable weak bound sits below the amplification threshold, or if the threshold argument itself relativizes and thus meets the contrary-oracle wall, the direction fails at the cost of one lemma. A second cheap check: verify the amplification does not smuggle in a large constructive property, which would re-enter the pnp-08 trap.

assumptions: a nondeterministic ACC0-SAT algorithm beating exhaustive search by superpolynomial savings is attainable
an algorithm-to-hardness bridge tolerates modest savings rather than full derandomization

proposal.structural_violation_claim: Every recorded attempt analyzed the model directly, seeking a broadly shared checkable property of all small circuits — the conserved model-analysis-first and large-constructive-property postures the weakened candidates name, and which the boundary deltas mark as collapsing the failure/success contrast. This direction instead analyzes an algorithm: design a slightly-better-than-brute-force satisfiability algorithm for ACC0 circuits, then convert its existence into a lower bound (e.g. NEXP not in ACC0) via an unconditional pipeline combining the recorded algorithm-to-hardness bridge with the recorded assumption-to-hierarchy-contradiction skeleton. No large truth-table property is exhibited, so the natural-proofs frame is not entered; the argument uses the anatomy of specific complete circuit-SAT problems, so it is not black-box query behavior. This is a hypothesized departure, not a verified construction, and not an exhaustive account of what the pipeline preserves.
proposal.novelty_argument: Not a relabeling of either parent. The recorded derandomization bridge consumes an open hypothesis (full deterministic PIT) it cannot supply; the recorded time-space pipeline is unconditional but refutes its assumed algorithm rather than supplying one, and stays largely relativizing. The hybrid changes the consumed object: it demands only a marginal gain over 2^n for a class sitting exactly at the recorded ACC0 stall edge, and supplies it rather than refuting it. The load-bearing move is the reversal of analysis direction (algorithm-first), which no recorded failure shares. Remaining obligations: (a) construct the modest ACC0-SAT algorithm, plausibly extending the polynomial-representation structure that gave AC0[p] bounds over rings for composite moduli; (b) prove the bridge lemma tolerates savings this small.
proposal.cheapest_falsification_path: (1) Bridge sanity: write out the implication skeleton for a toy class and check by hand whether the hierarchy machinery still yields a contradiction with only quasi-polynomial savings; if the bridge provably needs PIT-strength input, the direction collapses into the recorded conditional bridge and fails. (2) Relativization check: test whether the full implication survives substitution of a shared oracle; if it does, the contrary-oracle result condemns it before any algorithm is built.

assumptions: a satisfiability algorithm for ACC0 circuits beating exhaustive search by a superpolynomial factor is attainable
completeness translations convert circuit-SAT speedups into nondeterministic time-class collapses
the collapse contradicts a hierarchy theorem when a hard class is assumed to have small ACC0 circuits

proposal.structural_violation_claim: The recorded stall (pnp-06, pnp-09) is that no truth-table property distinguishing ACC0 from hard functions was found, and the derandomization bridge (pnp-11) consumes an open general-PIT hypothesis. The proposed move exhibits no distinguishing property at all: it converts a concrete algorithmic deliverable — a modest ACC0 circuit-satisfiability speedup, which requires opening the circuit's box only algorithmically — into a lower bound for a nondeterministic exponential-time function via the assumption-to-contradiction pipeline of pnp-12. It is a hypothesis that such a speedup exists; the remaining obligation is to actually construct the ACC0-SAT algorithm and to verify the implication chain (speedup implies NTIME collapse implies hierarchy contradiction) without gaps at the succinct-reduction step.
proposal.novelty_argument: Nearest recorded families: the derandomization bridge (pnp-11) and indirect diagonalization (pnp-12). It differs from pnp-11 because the consumed hypothesis is a restricted-model SAT algorithm — a strictly weaker and plausibly attainable demand than derandomizing general polynomial identity testing — and differs from pnp-12 because the hypothetical algorithm is to be supplied rather than refuted, with the refuted assumption instead being the circuit upper bound. It evades the natural-proofs frame (pnp-08) since nothing large or constructive over truth tables is exhibited, and evades relativization (pnp-02) because the SAT algorithm must exploit the gate-level anatomy of ACC0, which an oracle re-definition destroys. This is a change of which object carries the hypothesis, not a change of terminology.
proposal.cheapest_falsification_path: Attempt the algorithmic half first on the smallest subclass: seek a satisfiability algorithm beating brute force for depth-2 circuits with MOD-6 gates, where the composite-modulus obstruction of pnp-06 already binds. Independently, stress the implication half: check whether every link in the speedup-to-collapse chain relativizes; if the whole chain survives arbitrary shared oracles, the contrary oracles of pnp-02 refute the route as stated and the non-relativizing ingredient must be located or the direction abandoned.
